_README: Per-bill phrases used to write bill-specific questions and cues (2026-10-18, Cameron's expansion). what = the core provision as a noun phrase; gain = who benefits; cost = who or what bears the burden; local = something a town would see change; risk = what could go wrong, as a noun phrase; critic = a clause critics would say, starting 'it'; alt = a smaller alternative, as a noun phrase. All drafts for Cameron to rewrite.

BI01.what: co-official status for Ainu in willing towns
BI01.critic: it divides towns along ethnic lines
BI01.alt: a language-school fund with no land process

BI02.what: a national price floor for rice and dairy
BI02.risk: overproduction paid for by the treasury
BI02.critic: it rewards big farms and raises prices
BI02.alt: a temporary support fund for bad years

BI03.what: deregulated investment zones near Sapporo, Tomakomai and Hakodate
BI03.gain: new employers and the workers they hire
BI03.local: permits, wages and land use in the zone towns
BI03.risk: a race to the bottom on labor protections
BI03.critic: it carves out a second set of rules for the rich
BI03.alt: a single pilot zone with a review

BI04.what: an earlier Sapporo extension of the Shinkansen

BI04.local: stations and timetables along the line

BI05.what: new patrol vessels and radar on the Chishima islands
